summary: Explains that WinRM requires an encrypted channel: TLS (HTTPS, recommended, works with all auth) or message-level encryption via NTLM, Kerberos or CredSSP over HTTP. Shows forcing message encryption, and disabling the requirement only for debugging via AllowUnencrypted.
questions: Why does WinRM fail over plain HTTP with Basic auth?
Can I use WinRM over HTTP securely?
How do I force message encryption on top of HTTPS?
How do I allow unencrypted WinRM traffic for testing?
Can AD Certificate Services issue my WinRM certificates?

answer_card.title: WinRM encryption requirements
answer_card.answer_md:
WinRM refuses unencrypted channels. Options:

- **HTTPS** (recommended): works with every auth type; needs a listener cert (ADCS can issue one in a domain).
- **HTTP with NTLM, Kerberos or CredSSP**: these encrypt the payload themselves.
- To require both transport and message encryption:
  ```yaml
  ansible_psrp_message_encryption: always
  ansible_winrm_message_encryption: always
  ```
  (HTTP message encryption needs pywinrm>=0.3.0.)
- Last resort, dev/debug only:
  ```powershell
  Set-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Service\AllowUnencrypted -Value $true
  ```
  This exposes credentials and lets anyone on the network hijack the session.
